articles.title: Circular cities go ‘green’ by reusing things over and over again
articles.snippet: To cut their wastes to nearly zero, circular cities are launching projects to repair, reuse and recycle virtually everything.
articles.summary: Circular cities are launching projects to repair, reuse, and recycle almost everything. Their goal is to cut their waste down to nearly zero.

articles.title: Sliding down surfaces can make rainwater corrosive
articles.snippet: Water droplets can take on an electric charge when they slide across objects. Charged rain may start to eat through bridges, cars and more, new data show.

articles.title: Let’s learn about hydrogels
articles.snippet: These polymer-based materials can sop up a lot of water — making them useful for a wide array of tasks.
articles.summary: Hydrogels are polymer-based materials that can absorb a large amount of water. This ability to soak up water makes them useful for many different tasks.

articles.title: Sliding down surfaces can make rainwater corrosive
articles.snippet: Water droplets can take on an electric charge when they slide across objects. Charged rain may start to eat through bridges, cars and more, new data show.
articles.summary: Raindrops can pick up an electric charge when they slide across objects. This charged rain could become corrosive and damage things like cars and bridges.
